```{r}
library(haven)
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)
file <- "Case 31 Data_efcu_4.sav"
dat <- read_sav(file)
names(dat) <- toupper(names(dat))
# The cleaned file includes recoded variables; do not activate SPSS FILTER_$.
valid <- function(x, allowed) as.numeric(x)[as.numeric(x) %in% allowed]
one_t <- function(v, null=3) {
 x <- valid(dat[[v]], 1:5)
 tt <- t.test(x, mu=null)
 data.frame(Variable=v, N=length(x), Mean=round(mean(x),2),
 SD=round(sd(x),2), t=round(unname(tt$statistic),2),
 df=unname(tt$parameter), p=signif(tt$p.value,3))
}
gof <- function(v, allowed) {
 x <- valid(dat[[v]], allowed)
 counts <- table(factor(x, levels=allowed))
 test <- chisq.test(counts, p=rep(1/length(allowed),length(allowed)))
 data.frame(Variable=v, t(as.data.frame.list(as.list(as.integer(counts)))),
 Chi_square=round(unname(test$statistic),2), df=unname(test$parameter),
 p=signif(test$p.value,3), check.names=FALSE)
}
```

## Case Background and Objectives

- Employees Federal Credit Union (EFCU) commissioned a member survey to investigate borrowing decisions, service awareness, and operational performance.
- The case describes a random sample of 300 members; **128 usable cases** appear in the supplied cleaned SPSS dataset.
- Analyses use available valid responses for each question; two-sided tests use α = .05.

## R1 — Why Do People Join the Credit Union?

**Important limitation:** The assignment key assigns Q7 to R1, but the questionnaire defines Q7 as *opinions about rates paid on share/savings accounts*, not reasons for joining. The actual reasons-for-joining item is Q2, which is absent from the supplied cleaned dataset.

```{r}
kable(one_t("Q7_R"), caption="Proxy analysis specified by assignment key: recoded Q7")
```

- Q7r mean = 3.07, n = 118; no significant difference from the neutral midpoint (p = .196).
- This does **not** establish the reasons members joined; Q2 data would be required.

## R2 — Why Use Other Financial Institutions for Loans?

- Q8r: perceived credit-union borrowing rates (recoded, higher = more favorable).
- Q30: agreement that EFCU loan rates are lower than competing institutions.

```{r}
kable(bind_rows(one_t("Q8_R"), one_t("Q30")))
```

- Q8r is not significantly different from neutral at α = .05 (p = .058).
- Q30 also does not differ significantly from neutral (p = .416).
- **Limitation:** Q29 directly asks why respondents borrowed elsewhere, but is not included in the provided cleaned dataset; rate perceptions are indirect evidence only.

## R5 — Awareness of EFCU Services

1 = aware and used; 2 = aware but not used; 3 = unaware.

```{r}
service_vars <- paste0("Q",13:26,"_R")
service_names <- c("Regular share", "Special subaccounts", "Christmas club",
 "Individual retirement", "MasterCard", "Signature loans", "New car loans",
 "Late model car loans", "Older model car loans", "Household goods loans",
 "Recreational loans", "Share collateral loans", "IRA loans", "Line of credit")
service_counts <- lapply(service_vars, function(v) {
 x <- valid(dat[[v]], 1:3)
 tab <- table(factor(x, levels=1:3))
 test <- chisq.test(tab)
 data.frame(Variable=v, Used=unname(tab[1]), Aware_not_used=unname(tab[2]),
 Unaware=unname(tab[3]), Chi_square=round(unname(test$statistic),2),
 p=signif(test$p.value,3))
}) |> bind_rows()
service_counts$Service <- service_names
kable(service_counts[,c("Service","Used","Aware_not_used","Unaware","Chi_square","p")])
```

## R5 — Interpretation

- Regular share accounts have the highest reported use (83/128 = 64.8%).
- Signature loans and new-car loans are known but rarely used (104 and 99 aware nonusers, respectively).
- Line-of-credit loans show no reported use and 48/128 (37.5%) unaware respondents.
- All 14 equal-proportion goodness-of-fit tests reject a uniform distribution (p < .001); **this does not test overall awareness against a benchmark**.

## R6 — Operations: Statements and Privacy

```{r}
ops_cat <- bind_rows(gof("Q9_R",1:5), gof("Q10_R",1:5))
kable(ops_cat)
kable(bind_rows(gof("Q11",1:2),gof("Q12",1:2)))
```

- Q9r and Q10r: distributions differ from equal category proportions (both p < .001).
- Q11: 125/128 (97.7%) report statements are easy to understand.
- Q12: among 106 valid answers, 74 (69.8%) believe account information is maintained confidentially.
- Goodness-of-fit uses an equal-proportions reference, not a business performance target.

## R6 — Operational Attitudes and Overall Rating

```{r}
kable(bind_rows(lapply(c("Q31","Q32","Q33","Q34","Q37_R"), one_t)))
```

- Q31–Q34 agreement averages exceed neutral (all p < .001).
- The recoded overall operational rating (Q37r) averages 4.07/5, significantly above neutral (p < .001).
- The questionnaire's raw Q37 uses reverse direction; the analysis uses **Q37_R**, with higher values representing a better rating.

## Conclusions and Recommendations

- **R1:** Direct joining motivations cannot be established without Q2.
- **R2:** The available rate-perception measures are near neutral; the direct borrowing-reason question Q29 is missing.
- **R5:** Awareness is uneven, and several loan products are rarely used; target communication toward less familiar services.
- **R6:** Members generally report favorable operational perceptions, while privacy confidence has room to improve.
- Results describe the respondents and should not be interpreted as causal evidence.
